# `slack.import`

Materialize an agent-submitted batch of your OWN Slack messages (captured agent-side via the Slack MCP; never called from here) into the local slack_export directory. Authorship is verified server-side per message against the top-level author_id — a mismatch is dropped, never accepted. Accepts the {author_id, messages} envelope inline or via --file; the CLI also falls back to stdin if neither is given.

- **group:** `mutation`
- **posture:** `reversible`
- **CLI:** `operator-voice slack-import`
- **MCP tool:** `slack_import` (mutation — hidden unless explicitly enabled)

## Arguments

| name | type | required | help |
|---|---|---|---|
| `author_id` | `str` | optional, default=None | Your own Slack user id (self-asserted; verified per-message server-side) |
| `messages` | `json` | optional, default=None | JSON list of {channel, message_ts, time, text, author_id} — alternative to --file |
| `file` | `str` | optional, default=None | Path to a JSON file containing {author_id, messages} (CLI convenience) |

## Examples

```
operator-voice slack-import --file /tmp/slack-envelope.json
```

## Errors

| code | what it means |
|---|---|
| `invalid_arguments` | An argument was missing, had the wrong type, or wasn't one of the allowed choices — nothing changed. |
| `author_id_missing` | Your own Slack user id (the top-level author_id) is required — supply it directly, or via --file/stdin as part of the {author_id, messages} envelope. |
| `no_messages_provided` | No messages were supplied — provide --messages, --file, or pipe the envelope via stdin. |
| `import_file_not_found` | No file exists at the given --file path. |
| `import_file_not_valid_json` | The --file content (or piped stdin) was not valid JSON. |
